title: Within 20: bridging ten and fact families
summary: Fill the ten first, then put the rest. Add three numbers, swap the numbers round and find the four facts in a family.
guide: This studio is for Year 1. Your child works with apples and counters and answers by tapping a number. If they can't read yet, read the sentences to them.
The key strategy is bridging ten: for 8 + 5, 2 of the 5 fill the first frame (10), and 3 are left: 13. Subtraction goes back the same way: for 13 − 5, take 3 to get to 10, then 2 more.

When adding three numbers, first add the two that make 10. In addition you can swap the numbers round ({{term:commutative-property}}). 9, 6 and 15 are a fact family: 9 + 6 = 15, 6 + 9 = 15, 15 − 9 = 6, 15 − 6 = 9.

engine.instruction-cross: Tap an apple to cross it out.
engine.instruction-paint: Tap a counter to change its colour.

make-ten.title: Fill the ten first
make-ten.prompt: There are 8 apples in the box. Put the other 5 in the box. How many now?
make-ten.hint: The first frame has 10 spaces. 8 and 2 make 10. How many go in the second frame?
make-ten.success: Well done! 8 and 2 make 10, and 3 more: 13. 8 + 5 = 13
make-ten.why: Why do we fill the first frame first?
make-ten.model: Because 10 is an easy number. With 10 and 3 we know it's 13 without counting.

feedback.too-many: There are still apples on the plate. Tap them to move them to the box.
feedback.too-few: There are still apples on the plate. Tap them to move them to the box.
feedback.only-extra: 3 is only the second frame. Count the full frame too: 10 and 3.
feedback.stopped-at-ten: 10 is only the first frame. Add the apples in the second frame.
feedback.one-group: 5 was just the apples on the plate. Count all the apples in the box.
feedback.too-big: Too many. Start at 10 and count the second frame.
feedback.too-small: Too few. Start at 10 and count the second frame.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

back-to-ten.title: Back to 10 first
back-to-ten.prompt: We have 13 apples. Cross out 5 apples. How many are left?
back-to-ten.hint: First cross out the 3 in the second frame; 10 are left. Then 2 more from the 10.
back-to-ten.why: Why did we break 5 into 3 and 2?
back-to-ten.model: Because 3 takes us exactly to 10, and taking away from 10 is easy: 10 − 2 = 8.

feedback.marked-too-few: Cross out 5 apples. Count the crossed-out ones.
feedback.marked-too-many: You crossed out too many. Only 5. Tap an apple again to remove its cross.
feedback.counted-taken: 5 is the apples you crossed out. Count the apples without a cross.
feedback.counted-start: There were 13 at the start. We took 5 away, so fewer are left.
feedback.stopped-at-ten: 10 is after crossing out 3. You crossed out 2 more as well.
feedback.too-big: Count the apples without a cross again.
feedback.too-small: Count the apples without a cross again.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

three-numbers.title: Add three numbers
three-numbers.prompt: Three plates of apples: 4, 7 and 6. Put them all in the box. First put the two plates that make 10.
three-numbers.hint: 4 and 6 make 10. Empty those two plates first. Then the other 7.
three-numbers.why: We changed the order and added 4 and 6 first. Why didn't the answer change?
three-numbers.model: They are the same apples; only the order we put them in changed. 4 and 6 make 10, and 10 and 7 is easily 17.

feedback.too-many: There are still apples on a plate. Move them all to the box.
feedback.stopped-at-ten: 10 is just 4 and 6. Add the other 7 apples too.
feedback.two-only: That's only two plates. Count the apples from all three plates.
feedback.too-big: Too many. The full frame is 10; count the second frame.
feedback.too-small: Too few. The full frame is 10; count the second frame.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

swap.title: Swap them round
swap.prompt: 2 red counters and 9 yellow counters. What number goes in the box?
swap.hint: Count the row once from the red end and once from the yellow end. They are still the same counters.
swap.why: For 2 + 9, which is easier: counting on from 2 or from 9? Why?
swap.model: From 9. We say 9, then 10, 11: only 2 steps. Because you can swap the numbers in an addition, the answer is the same.

feedback.total: 11 is all the counters. We want the number that is added to 9.
feedback.same-number: 9 is already there. What is the other number? Count the red counters.
feedback.empty: Tap the number for your answer.

fact-family.title: A fact family
fact-family.prompt: We have 15 counters. Keep 9 red and make the rest yellow. What is 15 − 9?
fact-family.hint: A full frame is 10. 10 − 9 = 1, plus the 5 in the second frame. How many are yellow?
fact-family.success: Well done! 15 − 9 = 6. So 9 + 6 = 15 is true as well.
fact-family.why: Write four number sentences with 9, 6 and 15.
fact-family.model: 9 + 6 = 15, 6 + 9 = 15, 15 − 9 = 6, 15 − 6 = 9. All four are one picture: 15 counters, 9 red and 6 yellow.

feedback.wrong-colors: 9 counters should be red and 6 yellow. Look at the diagram below.
feedback.same-part: 9 is the red ones. We want the number of yellow ones.
feedback.whole: 15 is all the counters. Count only the yellow ones.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.
